hook: I waited too long to go to court. **Is it too late?**
hook_q: How long do I have to file a case?

slides.title: Miss the deadline, **case dismissed.**
slides.body: A suit, appeal or application filed after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, even if the other side never raises limitation as a defence.

slides.title: Common **time limits.**
list: Money lent: 3 years from the loan
Breach of contract (general rule): 3 years from the breach
Possession of immovable property based on title: 12 years
Executing most civil court decrees: 12 years
Consumer complaint: 2 years from the cause of action
slides.ref: Limitation Act 1963 · Schedule Art 19, 55, 65, 136 · Consumer Protection Act 2019 · Sec 69(1)

slides.title: Civil appeal? **90 or 30 days.**
slides.body: An appeal under the CPC to a High Court must be filed within 90 days of the decree or order. An appeal to any other court: within 30 days.

slides.title: The **first day** doesn't count.
slides.body: In counting the period, the day from which it runs is excluded. If the last day falls on a day the court is closed, you can file when it reopens.

slides.title: A **written acknowledgment** restarts the clock.
slides.body: If, before the period runs out, the other side acknowledges the liability in writing and signs it, a fresh limitation period starts from the date it was signed.

slides.title: Late? Show **sufficient cause.**
slides.body: A court may admit a late appeal or application (except execution applications under Order XXI CPC) if you show sufficient cause. Consumer Commissions can also accept late complaints for sufficient cause.
slides.ref: Limitation Act 1963 · Sec 5 · Consumer Protection Act 2019 · Sec 69(2)

caption:
Thinking of going to court? Check the deadline first. 👇

1️⃣ A case filed after the limitation period shall be dismissed, even if the other side doesn't object
2️⃣ Money lent or breach of contract: 3 years. Possession of immovable property based on title: 12 years
3️⃣ Consumer complaint: 2 years from the cause of action
4️⃣ Civil appeal: 90 days to a High Court, 30 days to any other court
5️⃣ A signed written acknowledgment of liability, made in time, starts a fresh period
6️⃣ Late appeals and applications may be admitted if you show sufficient cause

Source: Limitation Act, 1963 (Sec 3, 4, 5, 12, 18; Schedule Art 19, 55, 65, 116, 136); Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sec 69)
